question: What is the theological basis for asking saints in heaven to pray for us?

choices.A: Saints are alive in Christ (Mark 12:27), remain in the Body of Christ, and their intercession is more powerful than earthly prayer — Revelation 5:8 depicts them offering the prayers of the faithful before God
choices.B: The saints are unconscious after death and cannot hear or respond to prayer
choices.C: Prayer to saints is acceptable only because God is too busy to hear individual requests directly
choices.D: Only Old Testament saints can be asked for intercession; NT saints cannot

teaching.title: The Intercession of Saints
teaching.body: Catholic teaching on saintly intercession rests on: (1) The saints are not dead but alive — Jesus says God is 'not the God of the dead but of the living' (Mark 12:27). (2) They remain part of the one Body of Christ. (3) Revelation 5:8 shows the 24 elders offering 'the prayers of the holy ones' (saints on earth) to God — depicting intercession by the glorified. (4) If we can ask living Christians to pray for us (James 5:16), asking the more perfectly holy saints to pray is a natural extension. Asking saints to pray is not worshipping them; it's the same as asking a friend to pray.
